title: Pointers in C
content: A pointer holds a memory address: `int x = 5; int* p = &x;`. Dereference to read/write: `*p = 10;`. Null pointer: `int* p = NULL;`. Pointer to pointer: `int** pp = &p;`. `void*` is a generic pointer — must cast before use. Pointer arithmetic: `p++` moves to the next `int` (4 bytes). Array name is a pointer to its first element.

title: Dynamic Memory Allocation
content: Allocate on heap: `int* arr = malloc(n * sizeof(int));`. Initialize to zero: `calloc(n, sizeof(int))`. Resize: `arr = realloc(arr, new_n * sizeof(int))`. Always check: `if(arr == NULL) { exit(1); }`. Free: `free(arr); arr = NULL;`. Memory leak: not calling `free`. Double free: calling `free` twice on same pointer. Use Valgrind to detect leaks.

title: Structs & Typedef
content: Define: `struct Point { int x; int y; };`. Declare: `struct Point p = {3, 4};`. Access: `p.x`. With pointer: `struct Point* pp = &p; pp->x = 5;`. `typedef struct { int x; int y; } Point;` — now use `Point` directly. Struct size may include padding for alignment. `union` shares memory — size is largest member.

title: Arrays & Strings in C
content: Array: `int arr[5] = {1,2,3,4,5};`. Strings are `char` arrays with `\0` terminator: `char name[] = "Alice";`. `strlen(s)` counts without `\0`. `strcpy(dst, src)` — ensure `dst` is large enough (use `strncpy`). `strcmp(a,b)` compares. `strcat` appends. `sprintf(buf, "%d", n)` formats into buffer. Avoid buffer overflow — always bounds-check.

title: Functions & Prototypes
content: Declare before use (prototype): `int add(int a, int b);`. Definition: `int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }`. C passes by value — changes to parameters do not affect caller. To modify caller's variable, pass a pointer: `void increment(int* x) { (*x)++; }`. Recursion: each call gets its own stack frame. Limit recursion depth to avoid stack overflow.

title: File I/O in C
content: Open: `FILE* f = fopen("file.txt", "r");`. Modes: `r` (read), `w` (write/truncate), `a` (append), `r+` (read+write). Read line: `fgets(buf, sizeof(buf), f)`. Write: `fprintf(f, "%s\n", str)`. Read formatted: `fscanf(f, "%d", &n)`. Binary: `fread/fwrite` with byte sizes. Always check `fopen` result and call `fclose(f)` when done.

title: Preprocessor Directives
content: `#include <stdio.h>` (system) or `#include "myfile.h"` (local). `#define PI 3.14159`. Macro with args: `#define MAX(a,b) ((a)>(b)?(a):(b))` — always parenthesize. Header guard prevents double inclusion: `#ifndef MY_H #define MY_H ... #endif`. Modern alternative: `#pragma once`. `#ifdef DEBUG printf("val=%d\n", x); #endif`.

title: Bitwise Operations
content: AND `&`: mask bits. OR `|`: set bits. XOR `^`: toggle bits. NOT `~`: flip all bits. Left shift `<<`: multiply by 2^n. Right shift `>>`: divide by 2^n (arithmetic for signed). Set bit k: `x |= (1 << k)`. Clear bit k: `x &= ~(1 << k)`. Toggle bit k: `x ^= (1 << k)`. Check bit k: `(x >> k) & 1`. Useful for flags and performance.

title: Linked Lists
content: Define node: `typedef struct Node { int data; struct Node* next; } Node;`. Create: `Node* n = malloc(sizeof(Node)); n->data = 5; n->next = NULL;`. Prepend: `new->next = head; head = new;`. Traverse: `Node* cur = head; while(cur){ printf("%d\n", cur->data); cur=cur->next; }`. Free all: traverse and free each node. Doubly linked list adds a `prev` pointer.

title: Recursion in C
content: Every recursive function needs a base case to stop. Factorial: `int fact(int n){ return n<=1 ? 1 : n*fact(n-1); }`. Each call pushes a stack frame — deep recursion causes stack overflow. Max safe depth ~10,000–100,000. Convert to iteration with an explicit stack when depth is unbounded. Tail recursion: some compilers optimize it to a loop (`-O2`).

title: Variable Scope & Lifetime
content: Local variables are `auto` (stack, destroyed on function exit). `static` local: persists across calls, initialized once. `static` global: file scope only (hidden from other .c files). `extern` declares a variable defined in another file. Global variables: zero-initialized by default. Avoid globals — they make code hard to test. Use `static` to encapsulate module state.

title: Function Pointers & Callbacks
content: Declare: `int (*fn)(int, int);`. Assign: `fn = &add;` or `fn = add;`. Call: `fn(3, 4)` or `(*fn)(3, 4)`. Typedef for readability: `typedef int (*BinaryOp)(int, int);`. Used in callbacks: `qsort(arr, n, sizeof(int), compare_fn)`. Strategy pattern: pass different functions to select behavior at runtime. Foundation for event systems and plugin architectures.

title: Bit Fields in Structs
content: Pack multiple small values into one struct word: `struct Flags { unsigned int read: 1; unsigned int write: 1; unsigned int execute: 1; };`. Saves memory — useful for embedded systems or protocol parsing. Layout is implementation-defined (padding, endianness). Do not use `sizeof` on bit fields. Combine with unions to read the raw integer and individual fields.

title: Sorting in C
content: Standard library: `qsort(arr, n, sizeof(int), cmp)` where `cmp` returns negative/zero/positive. Compare ints: `int cmp(const void* a, const void* b){ return (*(int*)a - *(int*)b); }`. Bubble sort (educational): O(n²). Merge sort: O(n log n), stable. qsort is not guaranteed stable — use a secondary key in comparator for stability. For strings: `strcmp` in comparator.

title: Common C Safety Pitfalls
content: Buffer overflow: writing past array bounds → undefined behavior. Use `strncpy`, `snprintf`, `fgets` with size limits. Format string attack: `printf(user_input)` is dangerous — always `printf("%s", user_input)`. Integer overflow: `int` wraps around — use bounds checks or `unsigned`. Uninitialized pointer: use `= NULL` at declaration. Compile with `-Wall -Wextra -fsanitize=address` to catch issues.
